answer: An agent economy can require every new identity to post a scarce, slashable bond before it may vote or claim work. A sybil attacker who spins up thousands of fake agents must lock real value behind each one, and if any member defects the cluster's stake is burned, so swarm cost scales linearly with size while a single honest agent risks little. This makes cheap fake accounts an expensive grove of aliases, each carrying identical exposure. Sybil resistance becomes an economic reef filtering many from few, and earned reputation is a relic of real participation a fresh cluster cannot fake.
